newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended mostly firmer as surprised dealers found themselves with a successful Swiss government bond auction on their hands.
Traders had forecast the auction to go poorly, saying that the market was liable to be undermined by lack of demand for a tranche which will expire in January 2014.

But allocation for the tranche totaled 256 million francs, plus 300 million set aside for the Treasury's own tranche, making the amount a bit higher than the maximum 500 million dealers had expected. The tranche, with a 4-1/4 percent coupon was priced at 98.50 to yield 4.377 percent

"The tender went surprisingly well," one dealer said. He added institional investors may have been among the active bidders, given that the longer tranche offers a yield above the key 4.00 percent level.

The Treasury also allocated 314 million in another tranche, which matures June 2000. That tranche was priced at 106.90 to yield 2.217 percent at issue. The government is also reserving a further 300 million francs of that tranche for its holdings.
News Swiss consumer prices in March fell 0.1 percent versus February offered little impluse to a holiday-thinned market. Trade will be closed over Easter and reopen on Tuesday.
